result.question: How does Nvidia characterize the impact of export controls on its business with China?
result.answer: Nvidia characterizes the impact of U.S. export controls on its China business as already harmful and potentially worsening. The company states that its competitive position "has been harmed by the existing export controls" and that its competitive position and future results "may be further harmed, over the long term, if there are further changes in the USG's export controls" [0001045810-25-000023:item-1-p016]. Nvidia warns that if the U.S. government (USG) changes the rules again, it "may be unable to sell our inventory of such products and may be unable to develop replacement products not subject to the licensing requirements, effectively excluding us from all or part of the China market, as well as other impacted markets, including the Middle East" [0001045810-25-000023:item-1-p016]. The company notes that the USG "has changed and may again change the export control rules at any time and further subject a wider range of our products to export restrictions and licensing requirements, negatively impacting our business and financial results" [0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. Nvidia also says that any new control impacting a wider range of its products "would likely have a disproportionate impact on NVIDIA and may disadvantage us against certain of our competitors that sell chips that are outside the scope of such control" [0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. Beyond China, export controls have "already and may in the future encourage customers outside China and other impacted regions to 'design-out' certain U.S. semiconductors from their products," and have encouraged overseas governments to request that customers purchase from competitors rather than Nvidia, "harming our business, market position, and financial results" [0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. Nvidia further notes that export controls increase the risk of investing in U.S. advanced semiconductor products because by the time a new product is ready for market, it may be subject to new unilateral export controls restricting its sale, "resulting in excess inventory and purchase obligations as we recently experienced with the H20" [0001045810-25-000116:part-ii--item-1a-p013]. The company also highlights that export controls may disrupt its supply and distribution chain, since a substantial portion of its products "are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong" [0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035].
